claims.sentence: On 7 October 2026 the WHO issued its first global guidelines on obesity in children and adolescents, with one document for each age group.
claims.evidence: WHO news item dated 7 October 2026, 'WHO issues first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity'; two guideline documents (children, adolescents).

claims.sentence: The WHO published its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity on 7 October 2026.
claims.evidence: News item URL and title give 7 October 2026 and 'first global guidelines'.

claims.sentence: One guideline covers children aged 29 days to under 10 years and another covers adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.
claims.evidence: Publication page for children's guideline: recommendations for children aged 29 days to under 10 years; adolescent guideline covers 10-19 years.

claims.sentence: The WHO strongly recommends structured changes to diet, behaviour and physical activity for children and adolescents with obesity.
claims.evidence: Retrieved summary of the news item: 'strongly recommends structured dietary, physical activity and behaviour-changing interventions'. Whether the page itself says it for both age groups is from a blended summary.

claims.sentence: The WHO says management should aim for better health, functioning and wellbeing, not only weight loss.
claims.evidence: No retrieved WHO text mentions health, functioning and wellbeing as the aim beyond weight loss; the search explicitly found nothing on this.
claims.newSentence: The WHO says the foundation of obesity care for children and adolescents is access to comprehensive support for healthy eating, physical activity and sustainable behaviour change, not medicines or surgery.

claims.sentence: The World Health Organization (WHO) issued its first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity on 7 October 2026.
claims.evidence: News item dated 7 October 2026, first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity.

claims.sentence: The WHO describes them as guidance for health systems and health workers on delivering evidence-based, people-centred care.
claims.evidence: Retrieved text says 'evidence-informed recommendations'; 'people-centred care' and 'guidance for health systems and health workers' not seen in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: The WHO describes them as evidence-informed recommendations for managing obesity in children and adolescents.

claims.sentence: There are two documents: one for children aged 29 days to under 10 years and one for adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.
claims.evidence: Children's publication page: aged 29 days to under 10 years; adolescents 10-19 years.

claims.sentence: The recommendations cover diet, physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep, behaviour-change and digital health interventions, medicines, bariatric surgery, weight-management devices and combined approaches.
claims.evidence: Publication description: dietary interventions, physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep, behaviour changing interventions, digital health interventions, pharmacotherapy, bariatric surgery and weight-management devices, and multimodal interventions.

claims.sentence: The WHO strongly recommends structured changes to diet, behaviour and physical activity for children and adolescents with obesity.
claims.evidence: Summary of news item: strongly recommends structured diet, physical activity and behaviour change interventions.

claims.sentence: The WHO treats obesity management as more than weight loss, with the aim of better health, functioning and wellbeing.
claims.evidence: Searches for wellbeing/functioning wording returned nothing; the retrieved text does not say obesity management aims at wellbeing beyond weight loss.
claims.newSentence: The WHO says medicines, surgery and devices are not the foundation of care for children and adolescents with obesity; comprehensive support for healthy eating, physical activity and behaviour change is.

claims.sentence: It presents the guidelines as part of a life-course approach that sits alongside its existing recommendations for adults.
claims.evidence: Summary of WHO news/guideline: presented as part of a life-course approach alongside existing adult recommendations (blended summary; moderate confidence).

notes: Date 7 Oct 2026 on who.int; PAHO republished 8 Oct 2026 (paho.org/en/news/8-10-2026-...). Early development documents said 0-9 years; final says 29 days to under 10. The 'wellbeing' framing (c05, c11) is unsupported; recommend removing from keyPoints and body. Search summaries blend pages, so c12 and c04 are moderate confidence.
